analysis: The PR changes only scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py, an offline unittest that asserts properties of .github/workflows/ci.yml and the composite action. It changes no runtime provider code, coordinator contract, keys, attestation, or prefix-cache storage, so the canonical provider threat IDs (T-041, TB-007, TB-011 and similar) are not affected. Modified assertions (test lines ~232-266, 347-351, 704-708) now expect job runs-on to come from the route job outputs (fromJSON(needs.route.outputs.routes)[lane]) instead of a fixed blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-27 runner. They also expect per-shard route lanes (test-provider-1..3), a summary job routed the same way, and test-cluster-checks routed via route. The tests still assert no continue-on-error, persist-credentials: false on checkouts, SHA-pinned actions, cache saves restricted to push on master/dev (SAVE_CACHES), and no secrets.* in the cluster-metadata job. The gating test still requires every lane result to be success. These are retained or strengthened, with no weakening. The tests execute only fixed local scripts and temporary git repos and stubs, with no network or secrets. Security-relevant point for later passes, outside the supplied evidence: the routing job and the Darkbloom sandbox runner grant (a macOS sandbox 'when granted') live in ci.yml and the route script, which are not in this batch. Whether that routing to a non-dedicated runner could expose secrets or poisoned caches on a PR runs cannot be judged from this test file alone. The test does assert that PRs never save caches, which limits cache poisoning. The patch excerpt was truncated, but the full head text of the changed regions was visible. No finding.
